description: We are a two-person team interested in sound design, audio engineering, and music technology. Our project focuses on sonification: transforming scientific and environmental data into sound. We aim to explore how audio can make complex information more accessible and engaging through a creative combination of science, technology, and sound.
summary:
We developed Volcanic Data Symphony, a project that transforms raw geological data into an immersive musical track. Using the seismic event catalog of Mount St. Helens, we wrote a custom Lua script for the REAPER DAW. This script parses the CSV file and converts earthquake magnitudes directly into MIDI notes, where the data dictates the pitch and the velocity (impact) of each sound.
To address the "Earth Information Jukebox" challenge, we mapped this generated MIDI data to percussion and bass instruments. The resulting rhythm is not composed by a human; it is entirely driven by the chaotic, real-world seismic activity of the volcano.
This project is important because it demonstrates the power of sonification. It bridges the gap between science and art, making complex scientific data accessible to visually impaired audiences and proving that raw data can be transformed into a compelling auditory experience.
details:
Our project uses a custom Lua script developed for the REAPER Digital Audio Workstation. The script parses a CSV file containing the seismic event catalog of Mount St. Helens. It extracts the magnitude of each earthquake and directly converts it into MIDI notes. The magnitude dictates the pitch and the velocity (impact strength) of the notes. These generated notes are then mapped to percussion and bass instruments to create a rhythmic track.

The project demonstrates the power of sonification. By turning complex seismic data into music, we make scientific information accessible to visually impaired audiences. It proves that raw data can be experienced emotionally and artistically, bridging the gap between science and art.

We used Lua (for scripting), REAPER (DAW), and AI tools for presentation design. The creative factor lies in letting nature compose the music: the chaotic rhythm of the volcano dictates the groove of the track, turning unpredictable geological events into a structured musical piece.
